key_insight: A single high-resolution turbulent realization contains enough recurring multiscale structure to train a patch-based super-resolution model that reconstructs unseen flow fields with strong fine-scale fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-efficient path for turbulence modeling and CFD post-processing when full high-resolution training datasets are too expensive or scarce.
method: Train a WDSR network only on overlapping patches from one high-resolution homogeneous turbulence snapshot.
Predict super-resolved patches for new low-resolution fields at x32 and x64 scales.
Reassemble patches with Hann-window-weighted overlap-add to suppress seams and preserve continuity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved recovery of vortical structures, high-wavenumber energy, and multiscale statistics versus interpolation, with comparisons against WDSR trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 full snapshots.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on 2D homogeneous isotropic turbulence, so generalization to 3D, nonhomogeneous, or wall-bounded flows still needs validation.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
